output.summary: A small tree endemic to south-eastern Australia, the drooping she-oak has long, hanging branchlets with leaves reduced to small scales. Its barrel-shaped mature cones contain dark brown, winged seeds, and it can flower throughout the year.
output.edibilityNote: An 1889 account says bushmen chewed the foliage to relieve severe thirst, while children chewed the young cones, called “oak apples.”
